title: WISDOM Project - X. The morphology of the molecular ISM in galaxy centres and its dependence on galaxy structure
question: Investigate the physical mechanisms setting the morphology of the molecular ISM at molecular cloud scales in the centres of eighty-six nearby spiral and early-type galaxies.

data.angular_resolution: WISDOM: typically 0.1 arcsec (~30 pc, median 34 pc, range 0.06 to 0.66 arcsec); PHANGS: ~1 arcsec (~80 pc)
data.sensitivity: WISDOM median surface brightness sensitivity: 0.2 K (~14 M_sun pc^-2); PHANGS typical sensitivity: 0.17 K (~11 M_sun pc^-2)

what.value: PHANGS CO(2-1) strict moment-zero maps and galaxy properties catalogue

evidence.quote: To conduct our analyses we use the ‘strict’ moment zero maps contained in the PHANGS data release (i.e. moment maps created using masks based on emission detected at high confidence)
We directly use the galaxy properties for the PHANGS galaxies from the data release catalogue as described in (cite: 2021arXiv210407739L).
The distance to each galaxy is taken from the NED redshift-independent distance catalogue (cite: 2017AJ....153...37S).

what.value: Mean distances to Virgo and Fornax clusters

evidence.quote: We place Virgo and Fornax cluster objects at the mean distance to the cluster (16.5 Mpc and 19.9 Mpc respectively; (cite: 2007ApJ...655..144M; 2001ApJ...546..681T)).

what.value: Stellar masses from ATLAS3D, MASSIVE, z0MGS, C17, and 2MASS Ks-band relation

evidence.quote: We take the stellar mass of each object ($M_*$) from various sources: ATLAS$^{\rm3D}$ (cite: 2013MNRAS.432.1862C), MASSIVE (cite: 2017MNRAS.471.1428V), the $z$=0 Multiwavelength Galaxy Synthesis (z0MGS) project (cite: 2019ApJS..244...24L) and (cite: 2017GCN.21707....1C).

Where stellar masses were not available from literature sources we estimated them here from the $K_s$-band magnitude of each galaxy (from the Two Micron All-Sky Survey: 2MASS; (cite: 2003AJ....125..525J)) using Eq. 2 of (cite: 2013ApJ...778L...2C).

what.value: Star formation rates for WISDOM galaxies

evidence.quote: Star formation rates are taken from (cite: 2014MNRAS.444.3427D; 2016MNRAS.455..214D) and (cite: 2019ApJS..244...24L), and we assume an uncertainty in these of 0.2 dex.

what.value: Stellar velocity dispersions for WISDOM and PHANGS galaxies

evidence.quote: Stellar velocity dispersion measurements were collected from a range of literature sources (cite: 2001A&A...374..394V; 2007MNRAS.379.1249D; 2007MNRAS.378..163H; 2009MNRAS.400.2098P; 2009ApJS..183....1H; 2012A&A...544A.105S; 2013MNRAS.432.1709C; 2014ApJ...795..158M; 2015MNRAS.446.2837S; 2015MNRAS.453.1727D; 2015ApJS..218...10V; 2019MNRAS.483...57P)

Stellar velocity dispersions were taken from the HyperLEDA catalogue (cite: 2014A&A...570A..13M) or literature sources where available (cite: 2006ApJ...642..711L; 2006MNRAS.366..480G; 2009ApJ...690.1031B; 2013A&A...556A..98V; 2015MNRAS.451..859L).
The PHANGS galaxies have AGN classifications from (cite: 2010A&A...518A..10V; 2021A&A...653A.172S), and we checked if these known AGN show different ISM morphologies.

recipe.goal: Create moment-zero integrated intensity maps for WISDOM galaxies and extract central cutouts for PHANGS and simulated galaxies
recipe.method: For WISDOM, apply the smooth-mask technique to primary beam-corrected cubes (smooth spatially with Gaussian FWHM = 1.5x beam and spectrally with 4-channel boxcar, threshold at >3x RMS of smoothed cube, apply mask to unsmoothed cube). For PHANGS, extract the innermost 3x3 kpc^2 from 'strict' moment-zero maps. For simulations, take face-on projected gas mass surface density maps and apply a 10 M_sun pc^-2 cut.
key_parameters: spatial smoothing Gaussian FWHM = 1.5 x synthesised beam; spectral boxcar width = 4 channels; amplitude threshold > 3 x RMS noise; central region = 3 x 3 kpc^2; simulation threshold = 10 M_sun pc^-2
assumptions: Gas in simulations becomes primarily molecular above a surface density of 10 M_sun pc^-2.

recipe.goal: Estimate total H2 gas masses and central 1 kpc mean molecular gas surface densities
recipe.method: Convert integrated CO intensities in moment-zero maps to H2 mass within the ALMA field of view and mean surface density within an elliptical aperture of radius 1 kpc (accounting for inclination and setting non-detected pixels to zero).
assumptions: Milky Way-like CO-to-H2 conversion factor of 2x10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 (alpha_CO ~ 4.36 M_sun (K km s^-1)^-1 pc^-2), line ratios T_b,CO(2-1)/T_b,CO(1-0) = 0.7 and T_b,CO(3-2)/T_b,CO(1-0) = 0.3, and zero surface density in non-detected regions.

recipe.goal: Convolve moment-zero maps to a uniform physical resolution and compute non-parametric morphology statistics (Asymmetry, Smoothness, Gini)
recipe.method: Convolve moment-zero maps covering the inner 3x3 kpc^2 to a fixed physical resolution of 120 pc, mask using elliptical apertures containing 90% of the CO flux, and compute Asymmetry (180 deg rotation subtraction), Smoothness (boxcar smoothing subtraction with width sigma = 500 pc), and Gini coefficient.
key_parameters: convolved resolution = 120 pc; elliptical aperture flux threshold = 90% (+/- 5% for uncertainties); Smoothness boxcar filter width sigma = 500 pc; Asymmetry rotation angle = 180 deg
assumptions: Background correction terms for Asymmetry and Smoothness are negligible because statistics are applied to masked moment-zero maps.

recipe.goal: Correlate ISM morphology statistics with galaxy physical properties, bars, AGN, Toomre Q ratio, and stellar volume density
recipe.method: Compute Spearman rank correlation coefficients between non-parametric morphology indices (A, S, Gini) and galaxy parameters (M_*, sigma_*, mu_*, Sigma_H2,1kpc, Sigma_H2,1kpc/mu_*, M_H2/M_*, SFR, sSFR, SFE, rho_*, rho_*,q), perform KS tests for barred vs unbarred and AGN vs non-AGN galaxies, and calculate Q_*/Q_g.
key_parameters: significance threshold p < 0.05; gas velocity dispersion sigma_g = 8 km s^-1; axis ratios q = 1 (spherical) or q = 0.8 (ETGs) and 0.27 (spirals)
assumptions: Constant gas velocity dispersion sigma_g ~ 8 km s^-1 across galaxies; for WISDOM sources, mean gas surface density within R_e is estimated using total H2 mass and R_e.

recipe.goal: Determine optimal predictors of ISM morphology using multivariate linear regression and feature selection
recipe.method: Use univariate and multivariate ordinary least-squares linear regression and Sequential Feature Selection with cross-validation in scikit-learn on 12 observed parameters to find the optimal subset predicting A, S, and Gini.
key_parameters: 12 candidate features: stellar mass, effective radius, inclination, SFR, sSFR, SFE, Sigma_H2,1kpc, M_H2, mu_*, Sigma_H2,1kpc/mu_*, beam size in pc, beam size in arcsec
assumptions: Log-linear relations between non-parametric morphology indicators and physical parameters.

answer_key.quantity: Spearman rank correlation coefficient (Asymmetry vs Smoothness)

evidence.quote: Asymmetry vs. Smoothness | 0.72 | 2 × 10^−15^

answer_key.quantity: Spearman rank correlation coefficient (Gini vs Smoothness)

evidence.quote: Gini vs. Smoothness | 0.68 | 3 × 10^−13^

answer_key.quantity: Spearman rank correlation coefficient (Gini vs Asymmetry)

evidence.quote: Gini vs. Asymmetry | 0.61 | 1 × 10^−10^

answer_key.quantity: Spearman rank correlation coefficient (log M_* vs Asymmetry)
Spearman rank correlation coefficient (log mu_* vs Asymmetry)
Spearman rank correlation coefficient (log mu_* vs Smoothness)
Spearman rank correlation coefficient (log mu_* vs Gini)
Spearman rank correlation coefficient (log Sigma_H2,1kpc vs Asymmetry)
Spearman rank correlation coefficient (log SFE vs Asymmetry)
Spearman rank correlation coefficient (log rho_* vs Gini)
KS test statistic D for Gini between barred and unbarred galaxies

evidence.quote: The distribution of the Gini estimator does show significant difference between barred and unbarred galaxies: suggesting that the central ISM in barred galaxies is less smooth ($D=0.32$, $p=$0.01).

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of sample galaxies with Toomre Q ratio Q_*/Q_g < 1

evidence.quote: Assuming $\sigma_g$ is $\approx$8 km s$^{-1}$(e.g. (cite: 2013AJ....146..150C)), in Figure 8 we show that $\approx$75% of our sample galaxies have $\frac{Q_*}{Q_g}<1$, and thus the stability of their gas disc is dominated by that of the stellar component.

answer_key.quantity: RMS scatter of Asymmetry predicted by mu_* alone

evidence.quote: We find that $\mu_*$ is the single feature that can predict the Asymmetry parameter most strongly, with an RMS scatter of 0.29.

answer_key.quantity: RMS scatter of Asymmetry predicted by 3 optimal features (mu_*, Sigma_H2,1kpc, SFE)

evidence.quote: The third important parameter is the SFE, resulting in predictions with an RMS scatter of 0.25.

score_reason: The non-parametric morphology equations, resolution matching (120 pc), aperture definitions (inner 3x3 kpc^2, 90% flux ellipse), and tabulated galaxy/morphology values (Tables 1-4) are clearly documented, and PHANGS products are public, though some WISDOM maps were in prep and exact PA/inclination/bar tables are not printed.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA project codes and PHANGS data products are public, the mathematical definitions of Asymmetry, Smoothness, and Gini and the statistical analyses (Spearman correlations and scikit-learn regressions) are explicit, and complete numeric answer keys are provided in Tables 1, 2, 3, and 4.
